chunk_findings.detail: `_NOT_WITH_QUEUE` lists `message, keep, allow_dirty, allow_empty, branch`, but `--model` is also a landing-only flag (the non-queue branch passes it straight into `api.merge_item(..., model=a.get("model", "") or "")`, and the `queue add` branch never uses it). The stated intent is that "landing flags refused with --queue", yet `ddflow merge --queue --model gpt-x <id>` passes the clash check (since `model` is not in the tuple), takes the `queue_add` path, and silently drops the requested model instead of returning the `queue.add` refusal that `--message`/`--branch`/etc. produce. Either `model` belongs in `_NOT_WITH_QUEUE` (so it is refused like the other landing flags) or the intent text is wrong; as written the two disagree and the flag is silently ignored.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/lifecycle_cli.py:_NOT_WITH_QUEUE

chunk_findings.detail: `_NOT_WITH_QUEUE` omits `model`, yet `model` is a landing-only flag: in the same function it is only ever forwarded to `api.merge_item(model=...)`, and the queue path calls `api.queue_add(repo, a["id"], agent=agent)` without it. So `ddflow merge --queue --model opus <id>` passes the clash check (the list is `message, keep, allow_dirty, allow_empty, branch`) and silently enqueues, discarding the requested model with no refusal and no indication. This contradicts the change's own stated contract ("landing flags refused with --queue" / the constant's docstring "What a landing flag means nothing for once the item is only being enqueued") and the analogous handling of every other landing-only flag. Fix: add `"model"` to `_NOT_WITH_QUEUE` (or forward it), so the user gets the same refusal they get for `--message`/`--branch` instead of a silently no-op flag.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/lifecycle_cli.py:391 (`_NOT_WITH_QUEUE` / `merge_call`)

chunk_findings.detail: The test runs the CLI `merge T1 --queue` first (which performs a real `queue add` for T1) and then, on the *same* repo and same item, calls the MCP tool with `{"id": "T1", "queue": True}`, asserting `mcp == cli`. The two bodies both carry the queue-entry fields `position`/`state`/`queued`, so equality only holds if enqueueing an already-queued item is a silent no-op returning the original entry. Given the stated semantics ("enqueues the item (queue add)", with a fresh add yielding `position == 1` in the sibling test), a perfectly reasonable implementation either appends a second entry (MCP returns `position: 2` while the CLI body has `position: 1`) or refuses the duplicate — in the second case `Server(...).handle(...)` returns a JSON-RPC `error` object, so `reply["result"]["content"][0]["text"]` raises `KeyError`. Input demonstrating it: a repo where T1 was just enqueued by the preceding CLI call, then the MCP call above. The comparison is between two different queue states, so it does not establish the claimed "CLI and MCP bodies are equal" property and will fail (or be vacuous, if the MCP call is merely deduplicated) for a correct non-idempotent `merge --queue`; use a separate repo or a second fresh item for the MCP leg.

chunk_findings.detail: `_changes` builds its list from `W.git(...).out.splitlines()` stripped with `.strip()`, and `_select` then does `changed = set(_changes(repo, rels)); todo = [r for r in rels if r in changed]`. Git quotes paths that contain non-ASCII bytes (or `"`/`\`/control chars) in `--name-only` / `ls-files` output under the default `core.quotePath=true`, and the call is made without `-z` or `-c core.quotePath=false` (the code line-splits, so `-z` was not used). Concrete input: `ddflow chore commit docs/é.md -m msg` after editing `docs/é.md`. `CO.relative` yields the raw path `docs/é.md`, `CO.outside` passes, but `_changes` returns `'"docs/\303\251.md"'` (with surrounding quotes), so the membership test in `todo = [r for r in rels if r in changed]` fails and `_select` returns `O.nothing(KIND, "nothing to commit: docs/é.md match HEAD")`. The user's real modification is silently not landed; the same command works fine if the file is named with ASCII only.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/chore.py `_changes` / `_select` (`todo` filtering)

chunk_findings.detail:
`_expand` only treats an argument as a directory when `(repo / rel).is_dir()` is currently true, so an argument that names a directory which was itself deleted (or whose only changes are deletions under a directory that no longer exists in the working tree) is kept verbatim as a single "file" entry. `_changes(repo, ["docs/gone"])` returns the deleted files under it (`docs/gone/a.md`, …), but `todo = [r for r in rels if r in changed]` filters on the literal `"docs/gone"`, which is not in `changed`, so `todo` is empty and `_select` returns `O.nothing(KIND, "nothing to commit: docs/gone match HEAD")`. Concrete input: `git rm -r docs/gone && ddflow chore commit docs/gone -m x` reports "nothing to commit" although the deletion is a real change; naming the deleted files individually (`ddflow chore commit docs/gone/a.md -m x`) takes the same path through `_changes` and commits correctly, so the directory form is simply mis-handled.

(For completeness on the parts I could verify: the `outside` refusal is applied to the post-`_expand` list, so a directory argument that drags in a changed file outside `[chore].globs` is correctly refused; `_skip_gates`' `(outcome, gate)` vs `(list, "")` return contract is consumed correctly by `isinstance(skipped, O.Outcome)`.)
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/chore.py `_expand`

chunk_findings.detail: The person's approval is bound to `cfg.chore.globs` only, but the power to excuse a *skipped* gate — including, per `skipped_ok`'s own docstring, "a required gate, which a skip otherwise does not satisfy" — is governed by `cfg.chore.skip_gates`, which `approval_digest` never hashes. Concretely: a person approves `[chore] globs = ["docs/**"], skip_gates = []`; the digest is `content_digest("docs/**")`. An agent then edits the config (by hand, or `ddflow config --set` — both are explicitly named as edit vectors in this module's docstring) to `skip_gates = ["review"]`. `approval_digest` is unchanged because it reads `cfg.chore.globs` alone, so `standing()` still returns ok and `exemption()` still hands back an `Exemption`; then for any chore item whose diff lies under `docs/` and which recorded `it.gate_outcome("review") == "skipped"`, `skipped_ok(cfg, it, excused, "review")` returns `True` and the required gate is treated as settled. The module's stated guard ("editing `[chore].globs` … leaves the chore class unapproved", "there is no flag that grants it") therefore does not extend to `skip_gates`: the approval silently widens to gates the person never approved for skipping, with no re-approval and no agent refusal.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/chore.py:38 (`approval_digest`) / :114 (`skipped_ok`)

chunk_findings.detail: For a task that merely carries the `chore` tag but whose diff falls outside the list, `judge` returns `exemption`'s "not a chore: …" string as a *blocker* (`[why] if why else []`). The module's own contract says the opposite should happen: "the exemption is judged on the paths the item ACTUALLY changed, so a code change tagged `chore` is an ordinary task", and the intent says completion "excuses the reviewer … only when the actual diff is inside the list" — i.e. outside the list the item is an ordinary task that must obtain a reviewer, not one that cannot complete. Given an item tagged `chore` that touched `src/app.py` and then went through a full, human-approved review, `judge` still returns `["not a chore: src/app.py match no [chore].globs"]`, so the blocker is added and completion fails even though every normal requirement is satisfied. The failure message and the docstring read like a note ("not a chore"), but the value is placed in the blockers slot, making the tag self-poisoning rather than merely non-exempting.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/chore.py:108 (`judge`)

chunk_findings.detail: The tracked/untracked decision is made against the **index**, but the reset is made against **HEAD**. For a path that is staged but not yet in HEAD (e.g. the user ran `git add docs/new.md`, or `git add -p`, before the chore), `git ls-files --error-unmatch -- docs/new.md` succeeds, so the code takes the `checkout` branch, and `git checkout HEAD -- docs/new.md` fails with `pathspec ... did not match any file(s) known to git` — the error is discarded and the file is left staged in the primary index/worktree. The subsequent `merge_item` then hits `Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten by merge: docs/new.md` and `_failure("merge", ...)` is returned, i.e. the command fails precisely because of the local copy that the comment says this loop exists to remove (`left, they make the merge refuse over an untracked file or fight a modified one`). Concrete input: `[chore].globs = ["docs/**"]`, a granted standing approval, `docs/new.md` a new file, `git add docs/new.md`, then `ddflow chore commit docs/new.md -m "docs"` — the task is created, claimed and committed in the worktree, then the chore is abandoned mid-flight (task left open) even though the input was legal. A symmetrical case exists for a staged deletion (`git rm`): `ls-files --error-unmatch` fails, `unlink(missing_ok=True)` is a no-op, and the staged deletion still blocks the merge. The test should be against HEAD (`git cat-file -e HEAD:<rel>`), and any failure of the reset should abort with a clear reason instead of being ignored.
chunk_findings.location: ddflow/api/chore.py:_stage (the revert loop, `if W.git(repo, "ls-files", "--error-unmatch", "--", rel).ok: W.git(repo, "checkout", "HEAD", "--", rel)`)
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/chore.py:_stage (the revert loop, `if W.git(repo, "ls-files", "--error-unmatch", "--", rel).ok: W.git(repo, "checkout", "HEAD", "--", rel)`)

chunk_findings.detail: The primary's copies are destroyed before the merge is attempted, and nothing restores them when a later stage fails. For an untracked new file the branch unlinks the only user-visible copy in the working tree; if `merge_item` then fails (base branch advanced / conflict, or a non-`chore.skip_gates` gate is still pending and merge refuses) or `complete` refuses, the returned `_failure` leaves the user with `docs/new.md` gone from their checkout — the content exists only inside the item's worktree branch, which the caller must know to recover with `git show <branch>:docs/new.md`. Concrete input: `[chore].globs = ["docs/**"]`, working tree has untracked `docs/new.md`, base branch has diverged so the merge conflicts, run `ddflow chore commit docs/new.md -m x`: the file is unlinked from the working tree, then the merge fails. The reset/removal should be performed only after the merge+complete succeed, or a rollback of the working tree should be performed on the failure paths.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/chore.py:_stage (the `else: (repo / rel).unlink(missing_ok=True)` branch)

chunk_findings.detail: `exemption` is the function that actually grants reviewer-independence (it is the one that returns an `Exemption`, the object the completion records), but unlike `judge` it has no `it.kind == "task"` guard. The module docstring states the consumer path explicitly: "`services.completion` asks `exemption` whether the reviewer-independence rule applies." So for an item whose kind is anything other than `task` — the class the intent limits to "a task tagged `chore`" — but which carries the tag `chore`, has changed paths all covered by `[chore].globs`, and has a standing approval, `exemption` returns `Exemption(...)` and the reviewer is excused. Concretely: an item of kind `bug` (or any non-task kind) with `tags=["chore"]`, paths `["docs/readme.md"]`, and a previously approved chore list gets `(Exemption(...), "")` from `exemption`, whereas `judge` would have returned no exemption for the same item. The kind restriction is only enforced on the `judge` path, so whichever caller follows the documented `exemption` path lets a non-task out of review by tagging it `chore`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/chore.py:exemption

chunk_findings.detail: The single-line `--explain` blob in this golden transcript is replaced wholesale, and comparing the old and new values shows exactly two kinds of difference: the intended addition of `chore.globs` / `chore.skip_gates`, and one unexplained provenance flip — `lease.heartbeat_s = 300   [default]` becomes `lease.heartbeat_s = 300   [file]` (every other label in the blob is unchanged in both directions: `lease.ttl_s`, `worktree.enabled`, `gates.task_pipeline`, `session.brief_max_tokens`, `enforce.commit_without_lease`, `release.manifest_lint`, `export.documents`, `export.tables` stay `[file]`, `dedupe.on_match` stays `[env]`, `agent.id` stays `[explicit]`). The change's stated intent is the chore class — refusing files outside `[chore].globs`, `ddflow chore approve`, and excusing the reviewer/skips only for in-list diffs — and nothing in it touches lease heartbeats. So either the fixture was regenerated under a config layer that happened to set `lease.heartbeat_s` (in which case the pin no longer describes the committed config and is machine-dependent, so the transcript test will pass/fail on whichever layer the rerun uses), or the repo's config does not set it and the expected output is simply wrong: regenerating `--explain` will print `[default]` and this transcript will not match. Either way the assertion this fixture carries about where `lease.heartbeat_s` comes from is now unsupported; it should be reverted to `[default]` or accompanied by the config edit that makes `[file]` true.

The module's stated guard ("editing `[chore].globs` … leaves the chore class unapproved", "there is no flag that grants it") therefore does not extend to `skip_gates`: the approval silently widens to gates the person never approved for skipping, with no re-approval and no agent refusal.

chunk_findings.detail: For a task that merely carries the `chore` tag but whose diff falls outside the list, `judge` returns `exemption`'s "not a chore: …" string as a *blocker* (`[why] if why else []`). The module's own contract says the opposite should happen: "the exemption is judged on the paths the item ACTUALLY changed, so a code change tagged `chore` is an ordinary task", and the intent says completion "excuses the reviewer … only when the actual diff is inside the list" — i.e. outside the list the item is an ordinary task that must obtain a reviewer, not one that cannot complete. Given an item tagged `chore` that touched `src/app.py` and then went through a full, human-approved review, `judge` still returns `["not a chore: src/app.py match no [chore].globs"]`, so the blocker is added and completion fails even though every normal requirement is satisfied. The failure message and the docstring read like a note ("not a chore"), but the value is placed in the blockers slot, making the tag self-poisoning rather than merely non-exempting.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/chore.py:108 (`judge`)

chunk_findings.detail:
`todo` is computed by `_changes(repo, rels)`, which runs `git diff --name-only HEAD -- <rels>`; the named paths are passed as a **pathspec**, and git applies the pathspec to the tree walk *before* rename detection (this is exactly why `git log --follow` has to re-run a pathspec-free diff and rewrite the pathspec). A rename whose source lies outside the named paths therefore never appears at all: the destination shows up as a plain addition, and the deleted source is filtered out. Both `rels` and `todo` (the only inputs to the refusal check) then contain exclusively in-list paths, so the command proceeds.

Concrete input: `git mv src/app.py rules/app.py` in the primary, with `[chore].globs = ["rules/**", ...]`, then

    ddflow chore commit -m "move rule" rules/app.py

`_changes(repo, ["rules/app.py"])` returns `["rules/app.py"]` only (`git diff --name-only HEAD -- rules/app.py` is the addition; `src/app.py` is not in the diff because of the pathspec), so `CO.outside(cfg, ["rules/app.py", "rules/app.py"])` is empty and the verb commits instead of refusing. The working-tree diff does touch `src/app.py`, a path outside the configured list, which the operator note (contradiction #7, 2026-10-17, D-chore-class / D-reviewer-rule-chore-exception) says the verb **MUST** refuse — "including a rename INTO the list". The same hole covers a hand-made move (delete outside + new untracked file inside), since `ls-files --others` is equally restricted by the pathspec. To satisfy the requirement the check must be evaluated over the full changed-path set (e.g. a pathspec-free `git diff --name-only HEAD` / index-vs-HEAD, plus untracked), not only over `rels` and what the pathspec-limited diff returns.
chunk_findings.location: ddflow/api/chore.py:88 — `CO.outside(cfg, [*rels, *todo])` cannot see a rename *into* the chore list

chunk_findings.detail:
`_clear_primary` unconditionally resets every path found in `HEAD` back to `HEAD` (`git checkout HEAD -- rel`), including a path the user had deleted in the primary to have the chore record the deletion. If `merge_item` then fails, `_bring_back` only copies paths that exist in the worktree (`if src.exists()`); for the deleted file the committed worktree copy does not exist, so nothing is copied back and the file stays resurrected in the primary.

Concrete input: primary has `rules/old.md` deleted (tracked in `HEAD`), run `ddflow chore commit -m "drop rule" rules/old.md`; the commit is created, `_clear_primary` restores `rules/old.md` to `HEAD`, `merge_item` fails (e.g. the branch's change collides with an unrelated local modification), `_bring_back` skips the path because `wt.path/rules/old.md` is absent, and the primary is left with `rules/old.md` present again — the user's deletion is gone, and re-running the command now reports "nothing to commit" because the file matches `HEAD`.
chunk_findings.location: ddflow/api/chore.py:139 `_bring_back` — a merge failure does not restore a deleted chore file, so the documented "a failure costs no work" is false for deletions

chunk_findings.detail: The change downgrades the refusal that `judge` produced for a `chore`-tagged task that does *not* earn an exemption from a blocker to a warning. Concretely: an item of kind `task` carrying the `chore` tag whose diff touches a path outside the configured chore list (or whose changed files cannot be read) comes back from `CO.judge(...)` as `(None, "", ["<why>"])`. Previously `v.blockers += why_not` made `ddflow complete` stop; now `v.warnings += why_not` lets completion fall through to `_unsettled(cfg, it, excused=None, s, required)`. Such an item already went through the chore ceremony, so the gates it was allowed to skip — including the reviewer — have been recorded as skipped-with-reason on the item, which is exactly the state `_unsettled` inspects; with the new code the out-of-list chore is accepted as an "ordinary task" whose gates already have outcomes, i.e. it can complete without the reviewer the refusal existed to force. This contradicts the stated requirement that the verb "refuse when the diff touches any path outside the configured list, including a rename INTO the list" and the governing decision D-chore-class ("code changes always refused"). The new docstring in `judge` ("A tag that earns no exemption is a note, never a blocker: the item is an ordinary task") states the verdict rather than justifying it, and it is precisely the guarantee under review. [D-chore-class]
